page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU instance featuring an Intel x86_64 architecture with 8 shared vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. For storage, it includes a local 740 GB NVMe SSD. The primary accelerator is a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.3333 allocation and 16 GB of dedicated VRAM.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the average tier for its hardware class. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is measured at 1786.68, while the multi-core performance reaches 14175.12. Memory bandwidth tests show 784.94 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, 88.57 GB/sec for large-block reads, and 52.63 GB/sec for large-block writes. Single-threaded gzip compression achieves 27.58 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 40.69 GB/sec. Database operations via Redis SET achieve 14.91 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 11.53 GB/sec.

By utilizing a fractional GPU allocation of one-third of an NVIDIA A40, this instance offers a cost-efficient alternative to provisioning a full, dedicated GPU for workloads that do not require maximum compute density. However, because the CPU allocation is shared, CPU-bound performance may experience variability compared to dedicated instances. This configuration is well-suited for machine learning inference, small-scale model training, video encoding, 3D rendering, and database applications that benefit from GPU acceleration and fast NVMe storage.
description: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a Cloud GPU instance designed for workloads requiring moderate GPU acceleration and fast local storage. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 8 shared vCPUs, 40.0 GB of system memory, and a 740 GB NVMe SSD. Acceleration is provided by a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results indicate solid mid-tier performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU scores at 14175.12 and Redis SET operations reaching 14.91 million operations per second. The fractional GPU design provides a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated tasks without the expense of a full dedicated card, though the shared CPU allocation represents a potential performance tradeoff. This instance is suitable for machine learning inference, video transcoding, and database workloads.
